projects.name: hackathon-agent-os
projects.title: Hackathon Agent OS — multi-specialist hackathon automation
ai_ml_usage: 28 specialist agents with enforced tool/write boundaries
Per-agent model and effort selection for cost control
projects.architecture: Orchestrator + dependency-aware task graph dispatching 28 AgentSpecs through a thread-local ExecutionContext that enforces a tool allowlist and write scope. Handoffs are a typed tool call, not parsed prose. Dual backend: real Anthropic, plus a simulated one that drives the same tool layer for free deterministic end-to-end testing.
features: Negation-aware specialist selection from the full brief (28 -> 19-27 per project)
Artifact contracts: a 'completed' claim with no files on disk becomes FAILED
Parallel waves grouped by write-scope disjointness
Self-correction: re-queue once with the failure appended, then abandon
Provenance ledger + verify_claims lint so the pitch invents nothing
Real .pptx / .pdf / .zip generation with unconditional secret exclusion
Three memory layers with budgeted, targeted context digests
projects.outcome: Working. 63 passing tests; a 27-task synthetic hackathon completes in 7 waves producing 37 files including a real 7-slide pptx and a secret-free submission.zip. NOT yet validated against a live model — no API key in the build environment, so artifact CONTENT quality is unproven.

reusable_components.what: ExecutionContext: thread-local tool allowlist + write scoping. The core reusable idea.
Typed agent handoff + validate_against, which downgrades unearned success
Dependency graph with cycle detection, priority/value-density ordering, blocked propagation
AnthropicBackend (tool_runner, pause_turn, refusal fallback) + SimulatedBackend pattern
Secret + insecure-pattern scanners with placeholder discrimination
Terminal capability detection with ASCII fallback — fixes Windows cp1252 crashes
pptx/pdf/zip generation; build_zip excludes secrets unconditionally

lessons: Enforce agent boundaries in code, not prompts — allowlist + write scope + artifact contract
Separate the agent that tests from the agent that fixes, or reports go green instead of products working
A deterministic simulated backend over the real tool layer makes multi-agent systems testable for free
Pair parallel results with their task at dispatch; positional zipping breaks when work is regrouped
Keyword-based capability detection must handle negation or it staffs work the brief ruled out

projects.name: playhack-iit-guwahati
projects.title: PLAYHACK - ML Track, IIT Guwahati (Round 1)
ai_ml_usage: LightGBM binary classifier (Task A: injury yes/no)
LightGBM L1/quantile regression (Task B: onset day offset)
Hybrid per-sport median + learned correction (Task C: recovery duration)
projects.architecture: Offline batch ML pipeline. Single notebook as source of truth, exported to playhack.py + predict.py. Fitted models + config serialized to models/ for reproducible inference.
features: 30-day observation-window feature engineering with structural leakage guard
Threshold sweep with trivial-baseline reference points
Label-shuffle leakage test + adversarial train/test validation
projects.outcome: Submitted. F1 0.5194, recall 0.9994, onset MAE 2.683 (skill 0.6476), recovery MAE 2.944 (skill 0.0919). Self-estimated composite 0.4196 +/- 0.0032. Official placement unknown.

reusable_components.what: End-to-end tabular pipeline: windowed feature build, CV harness, multi-seed loop
Load-model-and-score inference script; clean train/serve split
Documented notebook; Section 5 leakage proof, Section 8 final pipeline
Pattern: sweep decision threshold against the COMPETITION metric, not the task metric
Pitch structure: EDA -> methodology -> validation -> results

lessons: Optimize the threshold against the scoring rule you are actually graded on, not the per-task metric
Prevent leakage structurally (truncate once at load), then prove it by rebuilding features from mutilated inputs
Report trivial baselines alongside your score so judges can size the delta
State explicitly when a reported composite is your own assumption and not the official formula

projects.name: claude-agent-scaffold
projects.title: Claude tool-calling agent scaffold
ai_ml_usage: @beta_tool decorator: type hints + docstring -> JSON schema
Anthropic server-side tools (web search, code execution)
projects.architecture: Single-process CLI agent. tools.py defines the tool surface; agent.py owns the loop, history mirroring, pause_turn restarts and typed error handling.
features: run_shell, read_file, write_file, edit_file, list_files, http_request
Workspace sandboxing - all paths resolved inside workspace, ../ rejected
30k-char tool-result truncation to protect the context window
Env-var substitution so secrets stay out of the transcript
Refusal fallback to a secondary model
projects.outcome: Working scaffold, not tied to a specific hackathon submission.

reusable_components.what: Drop-in tool surface + @beta_tool contract; add a tool by writing one documented function
Agent loop with history mirroring, pause_turn restarts, typed error handling

lessons: The docstring IS the prompt - summary line tells the model when to reach for a tool
Return an error string from a tool rather than raising, so the model can recover instead of crashing the loop
Truncate tool results or one cat of a large file blows the context window
projects.secret_scan: Clean as of 2026-09-04 - .env.example holds a placeholder key only.
